thread:
cheng: noticing a burst of kubelet-driven evictions on gpu-pool-2 this morning, all flagged as 'node network health check failure'
maya: same, saw ~12 evictions in 3 mins, mostly pods with annotated rdma=true
alex: are these the new p4d nodes in eu-west-1? we started rolling those last night
cheng: yes, eu-west-1a & b. kernel 5.15.80, mlx5 driver 5.14.0, jumbo MTU set to 9000 on ixgbe/ens*
olivia: can you paste a log sample?
cheng: sure:
```
May 14 08:12:11 node-ew1a kubelet[2345]: E05014 08:12:11.123456 2345 kubelet_node_status.go:xxx] node controller reported networkUnavailable for node node-0123: netprobe failed: probe packet loss=62% latency=12ms
May 14 08:12:12 node-ew1a kubelet[2345]: Evicting pod gpu/vision-infer-7 due to node network health check failure
```
maya: 62% packet loss seems spurious on our private VPC — internal perf metrics show <1% packet loss between the node pair
alex: could be RDMA/SM flattening packets or offload mismatch with jumbo frames causing the netprobe to mis-measure
raj: this matches a previous incident where mlx5 offloads + iperf probing caused false positives (see thread 1749162345) but i know you wanted a different fix this time
cheng: i disabled net-probe on a canary node (kubelet flag --network-plugin=kubenet? no, --node-status-update-frequency? actually the flag is --eviction-hard? not ideal). I toggled the probe endpoint in our node-local probe config to skip local RDMA interfaces and evictions stopped for that node
olivia: what's the config diff?
cheng: small daemonset patch on node-probe configmap:
```
probe:
  interfaces_exclude: ["ib*", "rdma*"]
  probe_timeout_ms: 500
  loss_threshold_pct: 80
```
maya: increasing loss_threshold to 80% seems large but better than noisy evictions
olivia: worried about masking real network issues, especially across east-west if a real outage happens
raj: agreed. proposal: for gpu-labeled nodes (gpu=true) in dedicated pools, relax netprobe thresholds + extend grace period; keep strict defaults cluster-wide
alex: alternative: make the probe use TCP handshake to kube-proxy health port instead of UDP ICMP-like probe. Might be less sensitive to offloads
cheng: tried tcp probe quickly, it reduced apparent loss but adds ~10ms to measurement, still within our 50ms SLO for node checks
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0598 (auto) — tag: network-health-false-evict
olivia: action items?
raj: 1) patch node-probe config for gpu pools to exclude RDMA interfaces and raise threshold to 80% (hotfix)
2) roll a tcp-based probe option to staging for 24h A/B (next week)
3) audit kernel/driver versions across eu-west GPU fleet and schedule driver bump if mismatch (chore)
4) consider kubelet change to expose probe reason in /metrics for easier triage
cheng: i've applied the config change to gpu-pool-2 canary (node-0123) and monitoring shows no further evictions in 40m. I'll start 5% rollout if stable
maya: cost note — if we start delaying evictions, we may keep noisy pods on bad nodes longer and burn gpu compute. but current false positives cost more (restarts + reprovisioning)
olivia: let's keep an eye on cost dashboard, add alert if GPU utilization dips >15% for >30m on affected nodes
alex: also tagging oncall to be aware: set temporary suppression for these netprobe alerts to avoid paging until hotfix done
oncall-bot: paging suppressed for channel eng-runtime for 2h (reason: hotfix rollout)
raj: i'll follow up with a PR for the tcp probe prototype and kubelet metrics change
cheng: thanks — i'll update the incident with logs and the canary result in 30m
maya: nice catch, could have been a lot noisier during peak traffic :thumbsup:
olivia: if this holds, we can include the RDMA interface exclusion as a modeled default for dedicated GPU pools in our infra docs
cheng: noted, adding to infra-runbook (will link here)
raj: any objections to backporting a small kubelet flag tweak to the 1.27 patch we run on these nodes?
alex: +1 for backport if low-risk
cheng: no objections, filing the backport ticket now
maya: thanks everyone
